note: Grants Bdo has issued that outlive one task. A standing grant is not a wider authority than a task grant; it is the same typed, scoped, budgeted, expiring grant, decided once instead of asked for each time. Every grant here is graded against contracts/authority-grant.schema.json and exercised only through scripts/sovkernel/authority.py. A grant at PROPOSED standing is inert: the evaluator refuses it, so writing a grant is never the same act as switching it on.

issue_rules.judgement_authority_note: JUDGEMENT authority may be issued by the owner alone. A grant claiming it from any other issuer is refused, which is what stops a participant minting its own right to ratify.
issue_rules.ratification_note: A grant moves PROPOSED -> RATIFIED only by Bdo's recorded acceptance of its decision record. Nothing in the loop may perform that edit for him. grant:standing-landing-loop was ratified on 2026-08-25 by Bdo's recorded instruction; decisions/0065-standing-grant-ratified.md quotes it and names what would revoke it.

grants.note: The standing authorization decided with Bdo on 2026-08-25. It lets an in-scope change be committed as a frozen candidate after repository checks, then lets that exact candidate reach main only after independent observation. The grant excludes its own registry and schema, so an exercise cannot widen itself. `repository.commit` and `repository.land` intentionally carry different evidence preconditions: commit establishes the immutable candidate subject; landing consumes independent evidence about that already-frozen subject. The VERIFICATION type still cannot ratify a JUDGEMENT claim. The budget is per exercise, not cumulative. docs/ remains inside scope because docs/documentation.html is a generated projection that can otherwise leave verification red.
